lead.title: Rice reads an insect's own digestive enzymes to launch immunity
lead.summary: Sucking insects inject RNases into plants to free nutrients, and this work shows rice turns those enzymes' leftovers into an alarm. The glycine-rich RNA-binding protein NIB1 binds 2',3'-cAMP, 2',3'-cGMP and the dinucleotide ApG>p produced by a salivary T2 ribonuclease of the green stink bug, then forms nuclear condensates that recruit the core immune regulator EDS1 and switch on defence. Applying any of the three molecules on their own elicits the same NIB1 and EDS1 dependent response, and the authors point to a possible link with the nuclease activity of TIR immune proteins. The paper reports mechanism and elicitor assays in rice, not field protection or a deployable trait.

notes.label: Plant science
notes.text: Two other papers today put phase separation at the centre of hormone control: KAKU4 condensates restrain jasmonate signalling in Arabidopsis, while NIB1 condensates do the opposite for immunity in rice.

notes.label: Biotech
notes.text: Defence chemistry is becoming engineerable from both ends, with CsbHLH92 raising citrus limonoids on overexpression and a three-target fusion dsRNA killing 69.1 to 93.4% of three rice pests in the laboratory.

notes.label: Prairies
notes.text: Two new oat grain cadmium QTL from 596 Nordic breeding lines explain 34.69% and 27.92% of the variation, which is relevant to oat growers facing tightening grain cadmium limits (my inference, the trials were Swedish).

plant.title: Rice NIB1 senses cyclic nucleotides made by a stink bug salivary RNase
plant.summary: The glycine-rich RNA-binding protein NIB1 in rice binds 2',3'-cAMP, 2',3'-cGMP and the dinucleotide ApG>p made by a T2 ribonuclease in green stink bug saliva. Binding promotes nuclear condensates that recruit the immune regulator EDS1 and activate defence, and applying the three products alone elicits NIB1 and EDS1 dependent responses. Sucking insects appear to betray themselves through their own digestive enzymes, although the work reports mechanism and elicitor assays rather than field protection.

plant.title: A ZmNAC41, ZmABC and ZmCP module gives jasmonate-linked resistance to southern corn rust
plant.summary: On infection by Puccinia polysora, the NAC factor ZmNAC41 directly activates the PADRE-domain gene ZmABC, whose product binds the cysteine protease ZmCP. Silencing any one of the three genes weakened jasmonate responses and rust resistance. Natural variation analysis found elite haplotype combinations of all three genes significantly associated with better field resistance, giving breeders concrete targets.

plant.title: A promoter InDel in ZmASB1 links root tryptophan, auxin and drought tolerance in maize
plant.summary: Profiling 18 free amino acids in the roots of 192 maize inbreds gave 118 metabolite QTLs and prioritised ZmASB1, the anthranilate synthase beta subunit, as a driver of tryptophan levels. A 5-bp insertion or deletion 178 bp upstream alters binding of the factor ZmDOF17, and overexpression lines grew more root and tolerated drought better while the mutant did worse. The favourable allele is enriched in modern inbreds relative to teosinte and landraces; the drought phenotypes are from seedlings.

plant.title: Citrus gained three genes to make limonoids, and CsbHLH92 switches them on
plant.summary: Metabolite profiling of 134 citrus and related accessions plus genomes of 12 species in the orange subfamily show limonin, nomilin and obacunone appearing with citrus-specific acquisition of CYP88A51, CYP716AC1 and limonoid furan synthase, while the upstream cyclase OSC1 is conserved. The factor CsbHLH92 directly activates these genes and its overexpression sharply raised limonin and nomilin. Phosphorylation by CsMPK7 damps it during leaf senescence, when pests are less interested in the leaves.

plant.title: A noncanonical peptide cut from the PSK3 precursor strengthens antiviral defence in tobacco
plant.summary: Peptidomics across three tobacco cultivars with high, moderate and no resistance to potato virus Y identified a peptide from outside the conserved YIYTQ motif of the PSK3 precursor. It rapidly activates MPK3 and MPK6 phosphorylation and a transient ROS burst, with NbSnRK2 and NbACS1 contributing, and both overexpression and external application raised resistance to several viruses. Disrupting the precursor increased susceptibility and shoot branching. PubMed carries only a November 2026 issue date.

plant.title: Root proton pumps help rice take up iron in alkaline conditions
plant.summary: Phosphorus deprivation raised plasma membrane H+-ATPase expression (OSA1 and OSA8), protein abundance and activating phosphorylation in rice roots, and eased chlorosis at pH 7.5 with more chlorophyll and soluble iron. OSA1 overexpression lines were less chlorotic under alkaline conditions, while osirt1, osirt2, osysl15 and osiro2 mutants were more so. The authors conclude that Strategy I-like proton extrusion matters for iron uptake even in a grass; the work is in controlled solution culture.

plant.title: A fungal phosphate regulator decides when Colletotrichum tofieldiae colonises roots
plant.summary: In a conditionally pathogenic C. tofieldiae strain, the effector NFC1 is controlled by temperature and by the host's internal phosphate status, and it promotes infection when phosphate is sufficient. Under phosphate starvation the fungal regulator CtPHO4 represses NFC1 and colonisation while turning on fungal starvation genes. Part of the machinery is shared with a beneficial strain, tying nutrient status to the switch between helpful and harmful lifestyles.

plant.title: The nuclear lamina protein KAKU4 restrains jasmonate signalling through condensates
plant.summary: Loss of KAKU4 made plants hypersensitive to jasmonate, with stronger root growth inhibition and higher pathogen resistance. KAKU4 associates with MYC2 and JAZ3 and undergoes phase separation into nuclear-peripheral condensates that stabilise JAZ3 and limit MYC2 DNA binding and transcription. Jasmonate drives proteasomal turnover of KAKU4 while MYC2 later reactivates it, forming a delayed brake. The work is Arabidopsis only.

plant.title: MdMYB1R1 activates MdMAPKKK18 to protect apple from trunk canker fungi
plant.summary: Proteomics of apple twigs infected with Valsa mali found 904 differentially expressed proteins, among them the strongly induced MYB factor MdMYB1R1. Stable overexpression in apple raised resistance to both V. mali and Botryosphaeria dothidea, while silencing impaired it. DAP-seq and reporter assays show it binds and activates the MdMAPKKK18 promoter, but that gene only partly rescued silenced plants, so additional defence pathways are involved.

plant.title: A 2.25 angstrom structure shows how an early streptophyte alga harvested light
plant.summary: Cryo-EM of a photosystem II, LHCII and LHCP supercomplex from a basal streptophyte reveals a nearly complete set of land-plant PSII core subunits, so much of that framework was in place before the move to land. Two ancestral LHCP monomers flank CP29 and bind an unusually high seven carotenoids each, including marine-type siphonaxanthin and siphonein that widen blue-green absorption. The LHCII trimer shows a chlorophyll macrocluster and a 96-femtosecond energy transfer step.

biotech.title: HiEGP folds environment data into genomic prediction for 1,421 soybean genebank accessions
biotech.summary: The authors assembled six breeding traits for 1,421 diverse soybean accessions across nine locations spanning latitudes 28.53 to 45.64 degrees, with bioclimatic and soil covariates. Their hierarchical framework reached average trait-wise correlations of 0.871 for untested genotypes in observed environments and 0.775 in unobserved ones, and 0.70 to 0.81 for 100-seed weight in an external USDA panel. Environment-response GWAS recovered known maturity loci and flagged 175 candidate regions, with some supported by mutant phenotypes.

biotech.title: Fusion-gene GM maize LD05 speeds stacking of insect resistance and herbicide tolerance
biotech.summary: Traits from LD05, a Chinese event carrying a fusion insecticidal gene and already holding a biosafety certificate, were introgressed into the elite inbreds Qixi5101 and DH382 by backcrossing with marker-assisted selection. The team reports better breeding efficiency than LCV01, which carries two separate insect resistance genes, and tolerance of four times the recommended medium dose of glufosinate. Hybrids Ludan509 and Denghai605 are said to hold their original yield, which is the developers' own assessment.

biotech.title: Two major QTL control cadmium accumulation in oat grain
biotech.summary: GWAS on 596 of 620 Nordic spring oat breeding lines, field tested in Sweden from 2015 to 2021, found two new grain cadmium QTL on chromosomes 3D and 4A explaining 34.69% and 27.92% of phenotypic variation. Effects that large suggest breeding could complement soil management as food oat demand grows. The same panel yielded 15 and 6 marker trait associations for thousand kernel weight and hectolitre weight.

biotech.title: The Tudor-domain gene CaTdp1 underlies pepper immunity to Phytophthora capsici race 3
biotech.summary: The inbred line ZCM334 is completely immune to races 1, 2 and 3 of P. capsici, and its race 3 resistance is controlled by a single dominant locus. BSA-seq and fine mapping in a near-isogenic line narrowed the interval to the single candidate CaTdp1, strongly upregulated 24 to 48 hours after inoculation, with SNPs and InDels in coding and promoter regions between immune and susceptible parents. Virus-induced silencing increased susceptibility.

biotech.source: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
biotech.title: Fusion dsRNA hits three rice pests at once and improves RNAi efficiency
biotech.summary: Screening in Tribolium castaneum picked three effective target genes, and a construct joining 200 bp of each silenced most stably with an LD50 well below single-gene dsRNA. A fusion dsRNA aimed at Nilaparvata lugens, Locusta migratoria and Sogatella furcifera killed 69.1%, 71.3% and 93.4% of them respectively, beating naked dsRNA, and was reported safe for the non-target organisms tested. Efficacy was measured in the laboratory, not in the field.

biotech.title: A rare mutation in CsCYP90A1 gives cucumber a super-compact architecture
biotech.summary: Mapping with 620 F2 plants placed the recessive scp-5 mutation in a 141.84 kb interval on chromosome 5, where an A to T change swaps a conserved lysine for asparagine in the brassinosteroid gene CsCYP90A1. The variant was absent from 382 cucumber accessions. Silencing reproduced the dwarf phenotype and brassinolide partly rescued it, which matters for high-density and mechanised cucumber production.

biotech.title: Editing DMP8 induces haploids in planta in fountain grass
biotech.summary: The authors report in planta haploid induction in Pennisetum alopecuroides by genome editing of DMP8, extending a system developed in maize and other crops to an ornamental and forage grass. Haploid induction lines shorten the route to doubled haploid inbreds, which is a bottleneck in outcrossing grasses. No abstract was posted with the PubMed record, so only the title claim can be reported here.

biotech.title: Chromosome rearrangements steer which wild-relative segments reach wheat
biotech.summary: The study reports that chromosomal rearrangements and sequence similarity drive preferential allosyndetic introgression from a wild relative into wheat, meaning alien segments do not enter the genome at random. That matters for pre-breeding, where unwanted linked material often travels with a target gene. No abstract accompanied the PubMed record, so the numbers behind the claim are not available here.

biotech.title: A peptide encoded inside rice pri-miR160 acts on immunity independently of the miRNA
biotech.summary: The authors report that miPEP160, a small peptide encoded in the primary transcript of rice miR160, regulates immunity and growth separately from miR160 itself. Peptides hidden in miRNA precursors are a young field, and a rice case with an immunity phenotype would widen the toolkit for engineering defence without changing the miRNA. PubMed has no abstract for the record yet, so this rests on the title alone.

biotech.title: Nineteen beet mitochondrial genomes map the sequences behind cytoplasmic male sterility
biotech.summary: Complete mitochondrial assemblies for 19 accessions covering sugar, table, fodder and leaf beet plus a wild beet ranged from 344 to 381 kb, with the wild beet largest and most repetitive, and all shared 53 core genes. The sterility-associated sequence preSatp6 appeared only in sterile lines and not in wild beet, and sterile lines showed faster substitution rates. The survey also found 809 plastid to mitochondrion transfers. Hybrid beet seed production depends on this cytoplasm.

ag.title: In-furrow Bacillus treatments lifted peanut yield 11.5 to 17.3% alongside chlorothalonil
ag.summary: Four field trials over three years in South Carolina tested commercial Bacillus products with strains D747 and QST713, two local B. amyloliquefaciens isolates and phorate, applied in furrow or as broadcast sprays ahead of standard chlorothalonil programmes for late leaf spot. In-furrow treatments did not cut disease incidence below chlorothalonil alone but significantly reduced defoliation and raised pod yield by 11.5 to 17.3%, while chlorothalonil alone gave no yield gain over untreated. Foliar Bacillus applications performed worse than chlorothalonil.

ag.title: Prothioconazole enantiomers degrade unevenly in wheat and paddy systems
ag.summary: Field trials in wheat and soil and in rice, paddy water and sediment tracked both enantiomers of prothioconazole and of its metabolite prothioconazole-desthio. R-prothioconazole degraded preferentially, so S-prothioconazole accumulated to enantiomer fractions up to 0.64 in wheat plants and soil and 0.56 to 0.63 in the rice system, while the desthio metabolite enriched to 0.67 and 0.72 in wheat and rice plants. Final residues in wheat flour, rice grain and rice husk were all below the 0.005 mg/kg quantification limit.

ag.title: Apple bitter rot fungi in Korea cross-infect walnut and black locust and stall above 35 degrees
ag.summary: Surveys of symptomatic apple fruit in four Korean provinces from 2020 to 2023 yielded 783 Colletotrichum isolates, with groups matching C. siamense and C. fructicola dominant among seven species confirmed by multilocus phylogenetics. Growth and lesion development peaked at 20 to 30 degrees, with upper 50% reduction temperatures of 29.66 to 36.58 degrees and nothing at 40 degrees. Cross-infection tests with 27 isolates showed two-way pathogenicity among apple, walnut and black locust, implicating orchard-adjacent trees in epidemics.

ag.title: Greenhouse whitefly uses pepper's own CaMYB73 to shut down flavonoid defence
ag.summary: Whiteflies preferred to settle and lay eggs on previously infested pepper plants, which had lower expression of phenylpropanoid and flavonoid genes and less total phenolics and flavonoids. Infestation strongly induced the R2R3-MYB factor CaMYB73, which binds a MYB cis-element in the CaPAL promoter and represses the rate-limiting enzyme of the pathway. Silencing CaMYB73 restored phenolic accumulation and significantly cut whitefly settlement and oviposition.

ag.title: Two medicinal plants resist root-knot nematode and could serve as rotation crops
ag.summary: Of 25 traditional Chinese medicine plant species screened, 23 were susceptible to Meloidogyne incognita by reproduction factor. Taraxacum mongolicum allowed high initial penetration and formed galls but produced no egg masses, with giant cell formation inhibited, making it highly resistant, while Plantago asiatica formed neither galls nor egg masses and was a non-host. A single microplot trial showed both reduced nematode populations in naturally infested soil, which the authors treat as supporting rather than conclusive evidence.

ag.title: Viewpoint: pot-based drought tolerance traits rarely scale to field yield
ag.summary: This viewpoint argues that pot protocols confuse survival under water limitation with sustained growth under it, and proposes defining drought tolerance as higher yield under water limitation in the field. It groups candidate traits into five hubs covering water demand, water budget size, speed of water use, water use efficiency and timing of use. It notes that a large body of work on oxidative stress traits never scaled to field yield, since potted plants and canopies face very different light and evaporative demand, and makes the case for agronomy as part of the answer.

ag.title: Methane oxidation in paddy soils feeds the microbes that make methylmercury
ag.summary: A survey spanning about 3,300 km of China's main rice areas found positive relationships between methane oxidation activity and the methylmercury share of total mercury, and between pmoA and hgcA gene abundances. Adding methane in microcosms raised methylmercury production by 40.7 to 177.7% and hgcA expression by 49.5 to 416.0% across three paddy soils. Stable isotope probing identified 112 mercury-methylating taxa taking up methane-derived carbon, apparently via handed-off intermediates such as malate and fumarate, which complicates methane mitigation in paddies.

ag.title: Simulations favour connected breeding for salt-tolerant rice in coastal deltas
ag.summary: Rice yield falls sharply above about 4 dS per m soil conductivity, yet genetic gains in salinity breeding programmes sit at 0.10 to 0.33% per year against the 1.5 to 2% needed for impact. A stochastic simulation of yield as an additive polygenic trait found that a connected breeding scheme sustained a higher late-horizon rate of gain than closed-pool genomic selection and retained 2.2 times more allelic diversity, with a 1.26 t per ha cumulative advantage that disappeared once resources were equalised. The authors stress that the simulation does not model salinity tolerance itself.

ag.title: A battery-free microneedle sensor reads plant nitrate using the soil to air temperature gradient
ag.summary: Polymer microneedle arrays were metallised and coated with nitrate-selective and reference membranes to form a potentiometric cell, giving near-Nernstian sensitivity of 50.84 mV per decade and a 32.5 s response, validated in lettuce and celery against ion chromatography. A thermoelectric generator driven by a 1 degree soil to air difference produced an average 44.45 mV, enough for repeated measurement and wireless transmission. It is a proof of concept aimed at better nitrogen management rather than a deployed product.

ag.title: A 114-year cultivation chronosequence shows erosion reshaping soil organic matter
ag.summary: Across Mollisols cultivated for 0 to 114 years, erosion ran at 440 to 4,800 t per square km per year, giving cumulative losses of 11,000 to 320,000 t per square km. Carbon to nitrogen ratios of particulate, mineral-associated and dissolved organic matter all declined, indicating faster loss of carbon than nitrogen plus fertiliser nitrogen inputs. The estimated microbial contribution to mineral-associated matter rose from 6% to 32%, although a Bayesian model still attributed 81% of it to particulate matter.

methods: Coverage window: 10 to 12 November 2026 (about 48 hours; the previous issue was 2026-11-10, so nothing was skipped). Items were found by PubMed searches filtered on entry date and by journal, plus three web news searches, and every item's date comes from the PubMed record rather than an opened publisher page: www.producer.com, growinagri.substack.com and www.sciencesocieties.org were all unreachable from this session, so no news item is included today and the briefing is journal-only. Four items (fountain grass haploid induction, wheat allosyndetic introgression, rice miPEP160, tobacco PSK3 peptide) have no abstract or only an issue-level date in PubMed, and are reported as title-level claims or dated to the PubMed entry; the beet mitogenome paper likewise carries an earlier article date with a November entry. The GM maize LD05 item is the developers' own assessment of their event. Arabidopsis-only results are flagged. No preprints surfaced in the window. Items already covered in the briefings of 6 to 10 November were skipped.
